# Contributing

Thank you for helping improve the Sign Language Mocap Archive. Everything here is released under [CC0](../LICENSE), so anything you contribute is released under CC0 too.

## Report a problem or request a sign

Use the [issue templates](https://github.com/StudioGalt/Sign-Language-Mocap-Archive/issues/new/choose):

- **Sign correction**: a motion shows a sign wrongly (handshape, movement, location, facial expression…).
- **File problem**: a file is missing, won't load, or imports wrong in your software.
- **Request a sign**: a sign that isn't in the archive yet. Please [search the gallery](https://studiogalt.github.io/Sign-Language-Mocap-Archive/) and the [open requests](https://github.com/StudioGalt/Sign-Language-Mocap-Archive/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20is%3Aopen%20label%3A%22sign%20request%22%20sort%3Areactions-%2B1-desc) first. If someone has already asked, add a 👍 to their request; the most-wanted signs are recorded first.

For questions, ideas, or to show what you've made with the archive, use [Discussions](https://github.com/StudioGalt/Sign-Language-Mocap-Archive/discussions).

Corrections are re-recorded under a new date. The old version stays in the repository so existing links and published work keep working, and the catalog marks it as superseded.

## Change the scripts or documentation

Pull requests are welcome for:

- `tools/`: the scripts that build the catalog, download packs, gallery and Hugging Face copy
- `Documentation/`: workflows, FAQs and the Blender pipeline scripts
- the issue templates and workflows in `.github/`

Please don't edit `catalog/` or `site/` by hand. They are generated by `tools/build_catalog.py` and `tools/build_site.py` when changes reach `main`.

Keep each pull request to one change, and say in the description how you tested it (for a Blender script, the Blender version you ran it in).

## Record an audit

Every motion gets an **animation review** before it's uploaded: someone checks it plays cleanly, with no gimbal flips, and looks about right. That review isn't recorded as an audit.

An **audit** is a separate check that the motion is correct as language. A third party, someone other than the people who recorded and cleaned it, verifies the signing: handshape, movement, location, orientation and meaning. **All motions are currently unaudited.** If you're a fluent signer, you're invited to offer audits and critique in [Discussions](https://github.com/StudioGalt/Sign-Language-Mocap-Archive/discussions).

An audit is recorded in the motion's ReadMe as `Audited by: <auditor> <date>`, and the catalog's `audited` column and the gallery pick it up from there. To record one, run this from the repository root, then commit and push:

```bash
python tools/mark_audited.py --by "Auditor Name" "SG ASL Robot 2026-11-19" "SG ASL Hello 2024-6-9"
```

You can name motions by catalog id, folder path or gallery link, or put them in a text file and use `--list checked.txt`. Add `--dry-run` to see the changes first. Auditors who aren't maintainers can open a pull request with the ReadMe changes instead, saying what they checked each sign against.

## Contribute motions

If you have sign language motion capture you'd like to add, please [start a discussion](https://github.com/StudioGalt/Sign-Language-Mocap-Archive/discussions) first so we can agree on the sign, the rig and the format.

Each motion lives in its own folder named `SG ASL <Sign> <Year>-<Month>-<Day> Upload`, filed under its collection and letter (for example `SG ASL Dictionary/ASL B/`). See [What's in a motion folder](../README.md#motion_folder) for the layout. Before a folder is added, check that:

- `Documentation/` has a ReadMe.txt whose first line is the folder's name without " Upload", with **Submitted by**, **Audited by** and **Model** filled in
- `FBX Files/Original/` has the raw take before cleanup
- no single file is over 100 MB (GitHub refuses larger files), and there are no Blender backups (`.blend1`)
- a redo of an existing sign has a newer date than the version it replaces, and sits next to it in the same folder

`tools/check_uploads.py` checks all of this for you. Run it on your upload folders before you add them; it uses the archive's existing versions to check redo dates, and also lists any standard exports that are missing:

```bash
python tools/check_uploads.py --dir "path/to/Ready for Upload"
```

The same check runs automatically on every push and pull request that changes a motion folder. If anything fails, the commit gets a red ✗ and the run's summary lists the problems.

## Code of conduct

Everyone taking part is expected to follow the [code of conduct](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).
